summary: Count up to 20 objects in a line, array or circle, and up to 10 scattered objects.
Explain that the last number said when counting tells how many, however objects are arranged.
Name the number that is one more or one less than a given number from 1 to 20.
Recognize pennies, nickels and dimes by name and know what each coin is worth.
Count to 100 by ones and tens, and count back from 20 by ones.
Count on from any number up to 100, and count back from any number up to 20.
Build and break apart 11 to 19 as one ten and some extra ones.
Read and write numerals 0 to 20 and match a numeral to a group of objects.
Compare two groups of up to 10 objects using greater than, less than or the same as.
Put together and take apart numbers up to 10 with objects and drawings.
Show addition and subtraction situations within 10 with objects, fingers, drawings or equations.
Solve add-to, take-from and part-part-whole problems within 10 using a choice of strategies.
Add and subtract within 5 fluently.
Make, continue and describe repeating patterns of shapes or numbers, and explain the rule.
Describe time patterns from daily life using words like yesterday, today, tomorrow, morning and evening.
Directly compare and order objects by length, height, width or weight and describe the difference.
Sort up to ten objects into categories, count each category, and order categories by count.
Pose questions and answer them from collected information and simple data displays.
Name, sort and compare flat and solid shapes of any size or orientation by sides, corners and features.
Describe where an object is using position words like above, below, beside and behind.
Model shapes seen in the world by building or drawing them.
Combine two or more simple shapes to make a larger shape.
Count forward and backward within 120 from any number; read, write and represent numbers.
Explain that a two-digit number's digits stand for tens and ones.
Compare and order numbers up to 100 with models, drawings and the symbols >, = and <.
Solve addition and subtraction problems within 20 using a variety of strategies.
Use pictures, drawings, equations and strings of related problems to build strategies within 20.
Use the link between addition and subtraction, treating subtraction as a missing addend, within 20.
Add and subtract within 10 fluently.
Decide whether addition and subtraction equations are true or false using the meaning of the equal sign.
Find the missing number in an addition or subtraction equation with three numbers.
Use properties such as order and grouping as strategies for addition and subtraction within 20.
Add and subtract one- and two-digit numbers within 100 using models and strategies.
Mentally find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number and explain why.
Add and subtract multiples of 10 within 100.
Explore and predict repeating patterns with up to three parts made of shapes, numbers or operations.
Create and describe growing, shrinking and repeating patterns by adding or subtracting 1s, 2s, 5s or 10s.
Estimate and measure lengths with non-standard units, then compare and order up to three objects.
Tell time to the hour and half hour, and find elapsed whole hours on a number line.
Know a quarter's value and compare values of pennies, nickels, dimes and quarters.
Ask and answer questions using collected data and graphs with up to three categories.
Identify, sort and classify flat and solid shapes by defining attributes, and build or draw them.
Combine flat or solid shapes into composite shapes and make new shapes from them.
Split circles and rectangles into two or four equal shares.
Explain a three-digit number's value as hundreds, tens and ones in different ways.
Count within 1000 by 1s, 5s, 10s and 100s, including backward, and by 25s from 0.
Represent, compare and order numbers to 1000 using place value and >, = and <.
Add and subtract within 20 fluently using mental strategies.
Find 10 more, 10 less, 100 more and 100 less than a three-digit number.
Solve one- and two-step problems adding and subtracting two-digit numbers with part-whole strategies.
Add and subtract within 100 fluently using place value and properties.
Tell whether a group of up to 20 is odd or even; write evens as doubles.
Use addition to total objects in arrays up to 5 by 5 and write a repeated-addition equation.
Make and describe number patterns formed by repeatedly adding or subtracting.
Make and describe growing and shrinking patterns using addition and subtraction up to 20.
Make a simple ruler from unit pieces and compare it with a real ruler.
Estimate and measure lengths and distances to the nearest inch, foot or yard with standard tools.
Measure how much longer one object is than another in standard units.
Ask and answer questions using collected data, picture graphs and bar graphs with up to four categories.
Show sums and differences of lengths on a number line diagram.
Tell time to five minutes with a.m./p.m.; find elapsed hours or half hours on a timeline.
Find the value of coin groups under a dollar, make amounts with coins, and solve money problems.
Describe, compare and sort flat shapes and solids like prisms and cones by attributes.
Find at least one line of symmetry in everyday objects.
Split circles and rectangles into halves, thirds or fourths and name the parts.
Recognize that equal shares of the same whole can have different shapes.
Read and write whole numbers up to 10,000 in standard and expanded form.
Compare numbers up to 10,000 using place value and >, = and <.
Round whole numbers up to 1000 to the nearest 10 or 100.
Describe unit fractions and build other fractions from them using wholes, sets, number lines and areas.
Compare two unit fractions using tools and strategies.
Show fractions, including ones greater than 1, in several ways.
Recognize and make simple equivalent fractions, including fractions equal to whole numbers.
Add and subtract within 1000 fluently to solve problems.
Solve addition and subtraction problems within 10,000 using equations with a letter for the unknown.
Describe, extend and create number patterns in multiplication and make predictions.
Show single-digit multiplication and division facts in different ways and relate the two operations.
Use commutative, associative and distributive properties to multiply and divide within 100.
Use the equal sign to decide whether expressions with addition, subtraction and multiplication are equal.
Multiply one-digit numbers by multiples of 10 from 10 to 90.
Solve real-world multiplication and division problems within 100 with models or drawings.
Solve multiplication and division problems within 100 with letter-for-unknown equations and justify answers.
Ask and answer questions using data, scaled picture graphs, bar graphs and dot plots.
Tell time to the minute and estimate to the nearest quarter hour from an analog clock.
Solve elapsed time problems using hour, half-hour and quarter-hour times within a.m. or p.m.
Measure lengths to the nearest half or quarter inch with a ruler.
Estimate and measure capacity, length and weight in customary units and solve same-unit problems.
Identify parallel and perpendicular segments and right angles in polygons and solve problems with them.
Classify and compare polygons, especially quadrilaterals, by properties; find quadrilateral faces on solids.
Find lines of symmetry in polygons.
Find a rectangle's area by covering it with unit squares without gaps or overlaps.
Find areas of rectangles and rectangle-made shapes by tiling and counting.
Discover that multiplying side lengths gives a rectangle's area.
Find perimeters of polygons, including missing side lengths, and solve perimeter problems.
Show that rectangles with equal perimeter can differ in area, and vice versa.
Read and write whole numbers through hundred-thousands in standard and expanded form.
Show a digit is worth ten times more than in the place to its right.
Compare and order multi-digit numbers using place value and >, = and <.
Round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.
Add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers fluently to solve problems.
Model and solve multiplicative comparison problems, such as three times as many.
Multiply up to four digits by one digit, and two-digit by two-digit, with arrays or area models.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by one-digit numbers, including remainders.
Solve multi-step whole-number problems with all four operations and check answers by estimating.
Explain and generate equivalent fractions, including those greater than 1, with models and number lines.
Compare fractions with the same numerator or same denominator by reasoning about size.
Compare fractions with different numerators and denominators using varied strategies.
Write whole numbers and fractions as sums of unit fractions.
Break a fraction into a sum of same-denominator fractions in more than one way.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators.
Find equivalent tenths and hundredths and add two fractions with denominators 10 and 100.
Write tenths and hundredths as decimals and decimals as fractions.
Compare two decimals to hundredths and record with >, = or <.
Generate number and shape patterns that follow a given rule.
Use input-output rules and tables to describe patterns and solve problems.
Find factor pairs for numbers to 100 and multiples of one-digit numbers.
Decide whether numbers are prime or composite using factor pairs.
Solve elapsed time and metric measurement problems, expressing measures in larger or smaller units.
Ask and answer questions using collected data and graphs.
Make dot plots of measurement data in halves, quarters and eighths.
Know angles as two rays sharing an endpoint; draw right, acute and obtuse angles.
Measure angles as parts of a 360-degree circle using division or missing factors.
Draw and identify points, lines, rays, angles, parallel and perpendicular lines, and symmetry lines.
Classify polygons by symmetry, parallel or perpendicular sides, angle sizes and side lengths.
Find area and perimeter of composite rectangular shapes with known side lengths.
Explain a digit is worth 10 times its value one place right, and 1/10 one place left.
Explain digit shifts when multiplying or dividing by powers of 10, using exponents up to 10^3.
Multiply up to three-digit by two-digit whole numbers fluently.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by two-digit divisors no greater than 25.
Treat a fraction as division and solve sharing problems with fraction or mixed-number answers.
Compare and order up to three fractions with unlike numerators or denominators.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators in word problems.
Model and solve problems multiplying a fraction by a whole number.
Explain how multiplying a whole number by a fraction above, below or equal to 1 changes it.
Divide a unit fraction by a whole number and a whole number by a unit fraction.
Read and write decimals to thousandths in standard and expanded form.
Compare and order decimals to thousandths using place value and >, = and <.
Round decimals to the nearest hundredth.
Add and subtract decimals to hundredths using varied strategies.
Write, interpret and evaluate simple whole-number expressions, with or without grouping symbols.
Generate two number patterns from two rules and compare matching terms in a table.
Plot ordered pairs in the first quadrant to represent problems and interpret the coordinates.
Solve real problems with units of distance, mass, weight, volume and time.
Ask and answer questions from data, dot plots and bar graphs, including an informal idea of mean.
Convert between metric units and use conversions in multi-step problems.
Convert between customary units of length, capacity and weight.
Classify, compare and contrast polygons by their properties, without building a hierarchy.
Show that attributes of a shape category belong to all its subcategories.
Find volume of rectangular prisms by packing unit cubes without gaps or overlaps.
Discover that base area times height gives a rectangular prism's volume and use it.

state_code: # - Georgia's K-12 Mathematics Standards (adopted Aug 26 2021, in classrooms 2023-24), CASE framework e9dd7229-3558-4df2-85c6-57b8938f6180 "Georgia's K-12 Mathematics Standards (SY2023-2024)":
#   https://case.georgiastandards.org/ims/case/v1p0/CFPackages/e9dd7229-3558-4df2-85c6-57b8938f6180 (element text + GADOE's standard-level isRelatedTo links to GSE/MGSE codes)
# - Georgia's K-8 Mathematics Standards (Aug 2021, with Evidence of Student Learning): https://lor2.gadoe.org/gadoe/file/1d6838d1-8779-4109-9e54-e179997dc18f/1/Georgia-K-8-Mathematics-Standards.pdf
#   (all 150 K-5 element codes in this PDF match the CASE framework exactly)

# - Explanation of Changes (Oct 2021; GSE references per standard): https://lor2.gadoe.org/gadoe/file/836e9559-396c-4feb-b0f1-7cdb47371678/1/Georgias-K-12-Mathematics-Standards-Explanation-of-Changes.pdf

# - Transition Support Document (Jul 2022; element-level GSE alignments for shifted content): https://lor2.gadoe.org/gadoe/file/2cda3401-c9ed-47f7-8fbc-354808bbce0b/1/GaDOE-Mathematics-Standards-Transition-Support-Document.pdf
# - Index page: https://gadoe.org/learning/mathematics/ (georgiastandards.org now redirects to a sunset page)
# - CCSS baseline: CCSS Math (corestandards.org); MGSE codes = CCSS codes with "MGSE" prefix and no cluster letter; cluster letters added here.
# STRANDS (Big Ideas, K-5): NR = Numerical Reasoning; PAR = Patterning & Algebraic Reasoning; MDR = Measurement & Data Reasoning; GSR = Geometric & Spatial Reasoning.
#   Excluded: MP (Mathematical Practices) and MM (Mathematical Modeling). Data & Statistical Reasoning (DSR) has no separate K-5 codes; it lives inside MDR.
#   Code = grade.strand.standard.element; standard numbers run across strands within a grade (e.g. 3.NR.1, 3.PAR.2, 3.PAR.3, 3.NR.4). Every K-5 standard has elements.
# - GADOE publishes GSE links only per standard (not per element); element-level ccss here = GADOE's standard-level links split by content judgement,
#   except where the Transition doc gives element-level alignments (1.MDR.6.2 & 2.MDR.6.1 -> 3.MD.1; 2.GSR.7.2 & 3.GSR.6.3 -> 4.G.3; 5.MDR.7.2 -> 6.SP.3).
# - kind is judged on content; strategy-choice wording (GA drops "standard algorithm") alone is not counted as a change.
# CCSS K-5 NOT COVERED BY ANY GA K-5 ELEMENT (dropped or moved up)
# - 2.MD.A.2 (measure one object with two units) - no GADOE link; dropped.
# - 2.MD.D.9 (line plot of measured lengths) - no GADOE link; dot plots start in grade 3.
# - 4.MD.C.7 (angle measure is additive) - GADOE says removed from grade 4.
# - 5.NF.B.6 (real-world multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers) - moved to grade 6 (GADOE links it to 6.NR.1).
# - Partly moved to grade 6: 5.NF.B.4 (fraction x fraction, area with fractional sides; only fraction x whole number kept in 5.NR.3.4),
#   5.NBT.B.7 (decimal multiplication/division; GA grade 5 keeps add/subtract only), 5.NF.A.1/5.NF.B.4 also linked by GADOE to 6.NR.1.
# - Partly dropped: 5.G.B.4 hierarchy of 2D figures (GADOE: hierarchy removed; 5.GSR.8.1 keeps classifying by properties);
#   5.MD.C.5c (volume of two joined prisms) not in any element; 4.MD.C.6 protractor measuring de-emphasized (protractors optional);
#   3.MD.A.2 metric units (g, kg, l) replaced by customary units in 3.MDR.5.5 (metric moves to 4.MDR.6.1); 2.MD.A.1/2.MD.A.3 limited to inches, feet, yards.
# - 3.NF.A.3d (compare non-unit fractions) moved to grade 4 (4.NR.4.2); grade 3 compares unit fractions only.
# - 4.NF.B.4 (fraction x whole number) moved to grade 5 (5.NR.3.4).
# - K.CC.C.7 (compare two written numerals 1-10): GADOE links it to standard K.NR.4, but no element states it (K.NR.4.2 compares sets of objects, words not symbols).
# - Money from K: K.NR.1.4 coin names/values (pennies, nickels, dimes), 1.MDR.6.3 quarters; marked "moved" from 2.MD.C.8 (judgement; CCSS only has money in 2.MD.C.8).
# - Patterning strand (new): K.PAR.6.1-6.2 (repeating patterns, time words), 1.PAR.3.1-3.2, 2.PAR.4.1-4.2 (growing/shrinking patterns), 3.PAR.3.4 (equal sign with multiplication).
# - Statistical reasoning cycle (ask a question, collect, analyze, interpret): "Ask questions and answer them..." elements K.MDR.7.3, 1.MDR.6.4, 2.MDR.5.4, 3.MDR.5.1,
#   4.MDR.6.2, 5.MDR.7.2; mapped to that grade's CCSS data standard where one exists (K.MDR.7.3 has none, so "new"). Grade 5 adds an informal mean (6.SP.A.3).
# - Elapsed time from grade 1 (1.MDR.6.2, 2.MDR.6.1), lines of symmetry from grade 2 (2.GSR.7.2, 3.GSR.6.3), parallel/perpendicular in grade 3 (3.GSR.6.1),
#   place value/comparison to 10,000 in grade 3 (3.NR.1.1-1.2), counting backward (K.NR.2, 1.NR.1.1), counting by 25s (2.NR.1.2), ruler construction (2.MDR.5.1).
# - Coins in K/1 marked "moved" (2.MD.C.8) rather than "new"; CCSS never states coin identification explicitly.
# - 3.G.A.2 (partition shapes into equal areas as unit fractions) is not in GADOE's links; listed under 3.NR.4.1 (area models of unit fractions) by judgement.
# - 2.MD.B.5 (length word problems): GADOE links MGSE2.MD.5 to 2.NR.3 (equal groups), which looks like an error; placed with 2.MDR.5.5 here.
# - 2.G.A.2 (rows and columns of squares) is linked by GADOE to 2.PAR.4; placed with 2.NR.3.2 whose evidence text explicitly includes it.
# - 3.GSR.6.1 linked by GADOE only to MGSE3.G.1, but its content (parallel/perpendicular segments, right angles) is CCSS 4.G.A.1/4.G.A.2; marked moved.
# - 3.NR.1.1-1.2 (read/write/compare to 10,000) marked moved from 4.NBT.A.2 (GADOE calls them additions to grade 3).
# - 3.PAR.2.2 (add/subtract within 10,000) kept "edited" of 3.NBT.A.2 with 4.NBT.B.4 listed for the extended range.
# - 1.PAR.3.2 / 2.PAR.4.1 overlap skip counting (2.NBT.A.2) but are framed as patterns; marked new.
# - 5.MDR.7.3 / 5.MDR.7.4 split CCSS 5.MD.A.1 into metric and customary, so marked edited (sub-part carve-out).
# - The CASE text of standard 4.NR.1 mentions comparing decimals; the 2021 PDF does not. Elements are identical in both.
